svg.title: Four stacked tiers under a ceiling. From the bottom: tier P, parametric, a finite catalog where only the values vary; tier R, relational, which selects, traverses and quantifies; tier A, aggregate, counts and ratios over those selections; and tier X, external join, data from outside the design. A dashed ceiling sits above them, and above that a separate box for analysis, which computes quantities rather than asserting over them. A rule may assert over a quantity analysis produced, by naming it, without crossing the ceiling itself.
svg.text: worst-case tolerance, timing, signal integrity: a different engine
the ceiling: everything below is one evaluation model

g.text: external join: data that lives outside the design
aggregate: counts and ratios over the selections
parametric: a finite catalog where only the values vary
every passive has an MPN from the approved list
test-point coverage of at least 95 percent
for every I2C net there is a pull-up to a rail
clearance, track width, via drill, pin-type conflicts

svg.text: the ceiling is not Turing-complete, which is what makes a declarative rules layer feasible
